jobs.title: Customer Success Manager, Enterprise Tech
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Join Anthropic's Customer Success team in a high-visibility & high-impact role driving AI adoption across a small number of enterprise accounts in our Enterprise Tech segment. As our dedicated Customer Success Manager for Enterprise Tech Customers you’ll be their partner and trusted advisor helping them harness the full potential of all our Claude capabilities - API, Claude Code, Cowork, and other surface areas.

You'll work with a book of global technology leaders to actively deploy AI and reshape the technology landscape. You’ll be working with key partners who are moving fast and pushing the boundaries of what's possible with LLM technology. Your role will entail developing genuine partnerships with the customer and key stakeholders, gaining a deep understanding of their multi-pronged business objectives, strategic direction, AI vision, and technical needs. You'll draw on both your business acumen and technical expertise to serve as a strategic advisor throughout their journey with us.

In partnership with the broader account team, you will help customers identify the right Claude capabilities for their specific business objectives, working closely with them to provide best practices and guidance while supporting them as their usage grows and evolves.

Your role focuses on helping customers scale their usage effectively, drive model and use case optimizations, implement change management strategies, and maximize the value of their investment through expanded use cases across their organization. The insights you gather from your customers will directly inform our research priorities, product development, and go-to-market strategies — making you a key voice in shaping how we build and deliver ongoing value as a business.

Responsibilities:

• Build trusting, strategic relationships with key customer decision makers in complex, matrixed organizations; understand their business and objectives and identify opportunities for optimization and expansion

• Own customer operations across the lifecycle of each account, maintaining a structured operational assessment (customer readiness, operational health, strategic alignment, enablement strategy, adoption intelligence) that grounds comprehensive account and success plans and Executive Business Reviews

• Become an expert in Anthropic's products across API, Claude Code and Cowork, understanding the technical nuances and best practices for each to guide customers to the right solutions

• Leverage your deep knowledge of each customer, and the patterns you see across your other Tech accounts, to proactively drive consumption planning and the value story behind it, developing credible ROI hypotheses and quantifying outcomes that build the case for continued and expanded investment.

• Monitor usage patterns and identify optimization opportunities across Claude surface areas (API, Claude Code, Cowork) to drive full value from contracted commitments

• Serve as the customer’s thought partner, enhancing their knowledge of Claude products by socializing Anthropic’s product roadmap, driving awareness on new products and engaging Product PMs

• Develop and execute change management strategies to drive end-user adoption and maximize value within customer organizations, including Train the Trainer programs, Center of Excellence development, and organizational enablement

• Ruthlessly prioritize across the account's many business units and workstreams, building programmatic, repeatable motions

You may be a good fit if you have:

• 6+ years of experience in Customer Success, Technical Account Management, Solutions Engineering, or Strategy Consulting

• Experience working with F500 technology companies, SaaS platforms, or digital-first businesses at the exec level—ideally including high-growth and established tech companies.

• You understand what it means to lead organization-wide change or adoption programs (multiple functions, hundreds of users) for a product that requires C-suite sponsorship

• Technical fluency with ability to understand and articulate AI/ML concepts, API integrations, and software implementation patterns across a set of diverse stakeholders—from developers and product managers to executives and end users

• Proven track record managing a portfolio of accounts while maintaining strong relationships and driving measurable outcomes — you can run multiple enterprise motions in parallel without letting any account go quiet.

• Cross-functional collaborator who represents the customer in a positive, proactive manner, rallying everyone around paths forward that solve customer needs

• Passion for AI and interest in responsible development of advanced systems. You have built with Claude Code, automating your own workflows with agents, skills, and tooling.

• A knack for bringing order to chaos and an enthusiastic "roll up your sleeves" mentality

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$200,000—$265,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Software Engineer AI Coding Tasks
jobs.description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works

• Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
• Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
• Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
• Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
• Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
• Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
• Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Requirements

• 2+ years of professional software engineering
• Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
• Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
• Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
• Regular use of an AI coding tool
• Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
• You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
• At least 10 hours a week, starting now
• A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

Nice to have

• Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
• Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

Terms

• US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
• Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
• The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
• Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

UL 508A control panel design experience

jobs.title: Virtual Intake Mental Health Therapist (Part-Time)
jobs.description:
The Problem

Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.

What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.

We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

The Problem

Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.

What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.

We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

Who We Are

Amae Health is a Series B, venture-backed Public Benefit Corporation that delivers specialty outpatient care for people living with severe mental illness, including schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar I disorder, and treatment-resistant depression. We design and operate high-acuity, in-person clinics across the United States.

Our model integrates psychiatry, therapy, primary care, dietitians, and community health workers under one roof to deliver coordinated, longitudinal care for a population that has historically been fragmented across systems.

Leading health systems collaborate with Amae to bring this model to their communities, including NewYork-Presbyterian, Cedars-Sinai, Mass General Brigham, Novant Health, and CommonSpirit Health. Our investors include health systems such as Cedars-Sinai and CommonSpirit Health, organizations that evaluated our model clinically and chose to back it.

Why We Are Different

Many clinicians who join Amae have worked in PHPs, IOPs, inpatient psychiatry, or community mental health. They understand the limitations of the traditional system. Amae was built to change that—for patients and for clinicians.

Integrated care, not a referral network. Psychiatrists, therapists, primary care providers, dietitians, and community health workers work side-by-side and share responsibility for the same patients.

Practice at the top of your license. Manageable caseloads, meaningful clinical depth, and purpose-built tools designed for this population.

Continuous learning. Through our partnership with Mass General Brigham, clinicians receive ongoing training, supervision, and mentorship in evidence-based SMI care.

Advancing the field. Our clinicians contribute to new outcomes frameworks and research shaping the future of severe mental illness care.

A model built for sustainability. Team-based care, thoughtful caseloads, and strong infrastructure make this work meaningful—and sustainable over time.

The Opportunity:

We are hiring a part-time (24 hours/week) Virtual Intake Therapist to serve as the clinical front door for prospective members across our California clinics. This is a fully virtual, licensed clinical role responsible for conducting comprehensive intake assessments and determining the right course of care for individuals living with serious mental illness (SMI).

Every person who reaches out to Amae for the first time will go through you. You'll conduct the clinical intake assessment — biopsychosocial history, mental status exam, risk assessment, diagnostic impression and level of care determination — and make the call: is this person a fit for Amae's integrated SMI care model, and if so, which clinic and care team should take them on? If not, you'll provide an appropriate referral rather than force a fit that isn't right.

This role centralizes and standardizes the intake function that today lives with individual Clinic Directors, giving prospective members a faster, more consistent front door across every California clinic.

What You'll Do:

• Comprehensive Virtual Intake Assessment - Conduct virtual biopsychosocial assessments, mental status exams, and risk assessments for individuals inquiring about Amae's services.

• Level of Care & Fit Determination - Determine whether Amae's integrated SMI care model is clinically appropriate for the prospective member, and determine their qualification to join our PHP or IOP programs. If they are not a fit, provide referrals to a more appropriate level or type of care.

• Diagnostic Impressions - Develop diagnostic impressions and preliminary treatment recommendations to hand off to the receiving clinic's care team.

• Clinic Coordination - Interface with Clinic Directors and care teams across California regarding patient appropriateness and readiness for programming, ensuring a smooth warm hand-off.

• Family & Referrer Communication - Answer questions from prospective members, their families, and referring providers about Amae's programs, and screen inbound referrals for appropriateness.

• Represent Amae’s Program - Engage potential members and their caregivers on what Amae Health’s program entails, what differentiates our outcomes, and how members might benefit from our program. Communicate our program effectively while ensuring the patient’s needs are met

• Documentation & Utilization Review - Maintain accurate, timely intake documentation, and coordinate with the utilization review/insurance authorization process.

• Overflow Clinical Coverage (as needed) - Provide occasional individual or group therapy coverage across California clinics during lower-intake-volume periods.

About You:

You've done real clinical intake work before and you're comfortable being the person who makes the call on fit and level of care. You ask good questions, listen for what's underneath the presenting complaint, and you're not afraid to say no to a referral that isn't right for Amae's model. You're organized enough to manage a full day of assessments without losing the thread on any one person, and you communicate clearly and quickly with our enrollment team and Clinic Directors so hand-offs don't drop. You're comfortable doing all of this over video, with the same rigor you'd bring in person.

What We're Looking For

• An active license to practice as a therapist in California (e.g., LCSW, LMFT, LPCC, or Licensed Psychologist), in good standing is required. Supervision hours are not available for this role.

• Master's or Doctoral degree in social work, psychology, counseling, or a related clinical field

• Prior experience conducting clinical intake assessments, diagnostic evaluations, and/or level-of-care determinations, ideally in a PHP/IOP, community mental health, or hospital-adjacent setting

• Direct experience working with serious mental illness (SMI) populations, including psychotic spectrum and mood disorders

• Strong working knowledge of risk assessment and crisis safety planning

• Excellent, fast, clear written and verbal communication — you'll be coordinating hand-offs with clinic teams throughout the day

• Comfortable and effective delivering clinical assessments over video/telehealth

• Highly organized, able to manage a full daily schedule of assessments without losing continuity

• Technologically savvy, with the ability to learn and navigate new tools quickly

What We’re Building

As a clinician at Amae, you are not adjacent to this work. You are essential to it.

• A national care delivery model for the highest-acuity patients in behavioral health.

• Precision medicine for SMI. Individualized treatment informed by multimodal clinical, behavioral, and social data.

• A clinical operating system that puts longitudinal data, real-time patient signals, and purpose-built tools into a single decision layer for care teams.

• Frontier science and measurement: defining and validating the outcomes frameworks that this field has never had. Hospitalizations avoided, days stable, functional improvement, and more.

• A partnership model with the country’s leading health systems that proves coordinated SMI care can work at scale.

What We Value

We center care in all we do. Empathy is not a brand value. It’s how we make clinical decisions, build products, and treat each other.

We challenge convention. The existing system is the problem. We question it, we test alternatives, and we move with urgency when something works.

We take the work seriously, not ourselves. High standards and humanity are not in tension. We hold a hard bar for quality while leaving room for humor and levity.

Your job isn’t done until the job is done. We close gaps, we follow through, and we don’t hide behind titles or org charts.

We win together and fail together. We own outcomes as a team. We learn fast. We don’t do blame.

We hustle with humility. Speed matters. So does integrity. We assume best intent and stay grounded in the mission.

Compensation & Benefits

Amae Health is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The pay range for this role is $58-$68 per hour and will be adjusted to market cost. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Parental leave and programs built around well-being. We’ll share specifics during the interview process.

If you want to practice at the top of your license, learn from the best in academic medicine, contribute to research that is defining a new field, and do it all inside a team that was actually built for this work, we’d like to talk.

What We Value

• We center care in all we do. Empathy is not a brand value. It’s how we make clinical decisions, build products, and treat each other.

jobs.description:
About Us: 

Homebound is on a mission to make it possible for anyone, anywhere, to build a home using technology. Created by an experienced team of construction, real estate, design, and technology experts, Homebound is transforming the residential construction industry by improving the costly and inefficient process of building a home. 

We’ve created an entirely new way to build homes with technology powering every stage from start to finish to provide a seamless experience for our customers. Homeowners across the country can choose where they want to live, select a home plan that’s perfect for them, then personalize and buy it, all online. Homebound has raised $150M in capital from leading venture capitalists like Google, Khosla, Thrive Ventures, and we’re scaling quickly in places like Texas, Colorado and Florida. Come build your future with us.


ROLE OVERVIEW

We're looking for a highly motivated, proactive, and detail-oriented Design Coordinator to join our Home Product Development team. This role is essential to supporting our designers, streamlining design operations, and helping implement the technology-driven processes that are transforming how Homebound designs and delivers homes.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter who takes initiative, learns quickly, and independently executes on responsibilities with minimal oversight. We're looking for someone who can learn a process, take ownership of it, and consistently deliver high-quality work without requiring ongoing direction. This individual should actively anticipate the needs of the design team, identify opportunities to improve workflows, and take pride in making the designers around them more efficient.

A significant component of this role will involve technology integration and implementation, particularly within Homebound's proprietary Blueprint platform. We're actively transitioning our design workflows, product catalogs, specifications, and documentation into this innovative system. The right candidate will be excited to work at the intersection of interior design, technology, and operations, helping establish and refine new processes as our platform evolves.

This is a collaborative, cross-functional role working closely with Design, Architecture, Technology, Procurement, Sales, Construction Operations, and external partners. Some travel may be required.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Design Team Support & Independent Execution

 - Proactively support designers by taking ownership of assigned tasks and executing them independently, accurately, and on time.

 - Anticipate team needs, identify outstanding action items, and follow through without requiring repeated reminders or direction.

 - Coordinate sample ordering, vendor communication, material sourcing, inventory management, and design studio displays.

 - Maintain organized physical and digital design resources, ensuring materials and information are readily accessible to the team.

 - Manage multiple concurrent priorities while proactively communicating progress, identifying roadblocks, and driving tasks through completion.

Technology Integration & Blueprint Platform Implementation

 - Play an active role in integrating design workflows, specifications, finish schedules, and product information into Homebound's proprietary Blueprint platform.

 - Support the creation, organization, maintenance, and quality control of digital product catalogs and design package documentation.

 - Work closely with Design and Technology teams to implement new platform capabilities, test workflows, and identify opportunities for process improvements.

 - Assist in transitioning existing design documentation and manual processes into standardized, technology-enabled workflows.

 - Develop a strong working knowledge of Blueprint and become a reliable resource for designers as new tools and processes are introduced.

 - Embrace evolving technology and processes with enthusiasm, adaptability, and a solutions-oriented mindset.

Technical Design & Documentation Support

 - Assist with reviewing and redlining interior drawings, including cabinet shop drawings, interior elevations, countertop drawings, and flooring diagrams.

 - Support rendering reviews by identifying discrepancies, coordinating redlines, and communicating design feedback to visualization partners.

 - Assist with maintaining accurate finish schedules, design specifications, material selections, and related project documentation.

 - Create mood boards, inspirational imagery, and presentation materials aligned with established design direction.

 - Coordinate with designers, vendors, and trade partners to ensure design intent and documentation remain accurate and consistent.

Design Studio & Operational Coordination

 - Support the setup, organization, and ongoing maintenance of Design Studios and physical material displays across markets.

 - Coordinate material samples and displays to reflect current product offerings and design packages.

 - Help establish scalable systems for sample management, documentation, and design operations.

 - Identify inefficiencies and recommend practical improvements that reduce administrative burden on designers.

 - Take ownership of assigned deliverables, deadlines, and performance expectations.


WHAT YOU BRING

Required Qualifications

 - 2–3 years of experience in design coordination, interior design support, project coordination, design operations, or a related role.

 - Demonstrated ability to work independently, take initiative, and follow tasks through to completion with minimal supervision.

 - A proactive, resourceful, and solutions-oriented mindset—you don't wait to be told what needs to happen next.

 - Strong organizational skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

 - Ability to quickly learn new tools, processes, and systems and apply that knowledge independently.

 - Genuine enthusiasm for technology, process improvement, and working within evolving digital platforms.

 - Strong communication skills, including the ability to proactively share updates, ask thoughtful questions, and escalate issues when appropriate.

 - Comfort operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment where workflows and priorities may change.

 - A collaborative, team-first attitude with a genuine desire to make the people around you more effective.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Background or demonstrated interest in residential interior design, architecture, or homebuilding.

 - Familiarity with construction documents, interior elevations, cabinet shop drawings, or technical drawing reviews.

 - Experience with Bluebeam or similar drawing review and markup software.

 - Proficiency with Adobe Photoshop, InDesign, or similar design presentation tools.

 - Experience working with digital product catalogs, design management systems, or technology-driven operational workflows.

 - Experience supporting the implementation of new software, systems, or standardized processes.

 - Familiarity with material sourcing, vendor coordination, and physical sample management.



Our Commitment:

We are focused on building a diverse and inclusive workforce. If you’re excited about this role, but do not meet 100% of the qualifications listed above, we encourage you to apply. To apply, please submit an application with your resume on the Career’s page. 

Homebound is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics or any other basis forbidden under federal, state, or local law. Homebound considers all qualified applicants in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.



Our Compensation Philosophy:

Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. jobs.title: Prototype Fabricator
jobs.description:
About the Company

We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

About the Job

Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention. The Node's turbo-generator system is the critical component which includes all components from the fluid interface through to encompassing electromechanical energy conversion, dynamic sealing, structural integration, and control interfaces.

As a Prototype Fabricator, you will support the manufacturing, machining, assembly, and integration of hydro turbines and generators. This is a roll-up-your-sleeves role in which you'll prototype, build, and troubleshoot alongside world-class engineers.

This role sits at the intersection of precision machining, electromechanical assembly, and innovative fixture design, supporting prototype builds as well as low-volume production. You will work closely with motor/generator engineers, fluid dynamicists, mechanical engineers and highly skilled electrical technicians to translate designs into robust, manufacturable hardware, ultimately ending in its deployment in the Node at sea.

Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis. If you are an excellent technician, regardless of your background, we want you to apply.

We strive to be the best engineering team on the planet and we compensate our team accordingly.

Responsibilities

• Operate traditional machines such as mill, lathe, saws, shears, press brakes, rollers, drill presses, grinders, plasma cutters, and related fabrication equipment

• Perform field-fit modifications, repairs, and rework on prototype and production hydro-turbine and generator subassemblies, precision rotating machinery, sealing interfaces, and related integration tooling

• Support trial builds, teardowns, re-assembly and design iterations

• Interpret and work from detailed manufacturing drawings and CAD models

• Collaborate with design engineers to suggest manufacturability improvements

• Design, fabricate, and validate custom assembly fixtures, jigs, and alignment tools

• Utilize 3D printing for rapid prototyping of fixtures and mock-ups

• Perform dimensional inspections using Vernier Calipers, micrometers, bore gauges, Dial indicators, height gauges etc.

• Ensure compliance with tolerance stack-ups during assembly

• Document assembly procedures, inspection reports, and deviations

• Provide feedback on assembly challenges, tolerance feasibility and fixture effectiveness

• Support prototype iteration cycles and root-cause analysis

• Contribute ideas to improve build repeatability, safety, and efficiency

Required Qualifications

• 5+ years of hands-on experience in prototype fabrication, metal fabrication, welding, or a related trade

• Demonstrated ability to fabricate one-off and low-volume assemblies from drawings, CAD models, sketches, and verbal direction

• Working knowledge of GD&T and tolerance interpretation

• Experience using 3D printing for functional prototyping or tooling

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Able to independently work on complex fixtures and assembly designs

• Strong problem-solving and hands-on troubleshooting ability

• High technical curiosity and a passion for learning

• Innovative mindset, comfortable designing solutions when standard tools don’t exist

• High attention to detail and craftsmanship

• Strong organizational and interpersonal skills

Desired Qualifications

• 10+ years in a similar role

• Experience operating and supporting multi-axis CNC machines for shafts, turbine runners, fixtures, tooling etc.

• Proficiency in TIG and MIG welding, preferably with stainless steel, aluminum, and carbon steel

• Experience fabricating, repairing, and finishing fiberglass components using molds, hand layup, vacuum bagging, resin systems, and composite bonding techniques

• Experience assembling high-precision rotating machinery

• Experience working alongside R&D teams in iterative development environments

• Experience working on marine or offshore machinery

• Experience working on subsea bearings, or hydrodynamic bearings, or hydrostatic bearings

• Experience working on laser cutting and laser welding processes

• Experience with instrumentation and controls (pressure transducers, thermocouples, RTDs, etc.)

• Familiarity with NX/Teamcenter

• Familiarity with materials and coatings for submerged or corrosive environments

• Familiarity with magnetic components and magnet safety

• Basic understanding of hydro turbines and electrical machines (stators, windings, insulation systems)

The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

Additional Requirements

• Travel to vendors and test sites as needed

• Intermittently able to work longer hours and weekends to support critical needs. While we expect a lot of each other, we also offer a high degree of autonomy and work-life balance, including flexiblePTO and flexible working hours.

Compensation and Benefits

If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

• Cash compensation of $45-55/hour.

• Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

• A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including: Flexible paid time off Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled) Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

• Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

Location

This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in Portland, Oregon.

jobs.description:
About the California Academy of Sciences

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—our mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

Our living collection reflects Earth’s vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Our research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi,  spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Our diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Whether you're conducting research behind the scenes or engaging the public on the museum floor, your work will help connect people to the natural world and empower them to protect it.

jobs.title: Tabletop Exercise Lead, The Anthropic Institute
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Anthropic Institute

The Anthropic Institute (TAI) is a function within Anthropic that works to advance the public conversation around AI.

The Institute is comprised of research teams tackling some of AI's most consequential societal challenges: the Frontier Red Team, which stress tests our systems against catastrophic risks; Societal Impacts, which studies how Claude is used by millions of people; Economic Research, which tracks AI's impact on people's jobs and the larger economy; the Rule of Law team, which studies AI's impacts to democracy; and more.

The Institute's mission is to reduce information asymmetries between Anthropic and the outside world, name and answer the hard questions implied by powerful AI systems, and publish these findings so that policymakers, researchers, technology leaders, and the public can reckon with what's here and what's to come.

About the role

The role. You will build and lead the Institute’s tabletop exercise program and the team that runs it. Based on trends visible in the exponential and in consultation with technical experts, you will set the research agenda: which questions the exercises should answer, which scenarios to run, with which audiences, and what each run is meant to test. You will own the methods that make results comparable across runs and turn them into findings people outside the room can use. You will hire and manage a team plus a bench of facilitators, and you will be the program’s public voice.

Why tabletop exercises? If RSI arrives, the hardest problems will be about making decisions under uncertainty. The people making them may not trust each other, and the authorities they work under may not be fit-for-purpose. A tabletop exercise (TTX) allows the people who would face that situation practice it before it is real. It also shows us what tools and information they reach for, including what they would need that does not exist yet.

Tabletop exercises are also a research method. You can run the same scenario many times, with different groups of people (and with many more AI agents playing in silico), and you start to see the distribution of decisions people make. This is one of the few ways to generate empirical evidence about the future, i.e., how people and institutions will respond to situations that have not happened yet.

Key responsibilities

• Set the program’s research agenda: the questions exercises should answer, the scenarios to run, and the audience for each

• Design exercises as empirical studies: define what each run tests, standardize scenarios and data capture so results are comparable, and use repeated play to map the range of outcomes

• Build the program’s measurement: pre- and post-exercise assessments, decision logs, transcript analysis and after-action reports

• Turn results into findings: publish on what the exercises show, and brief senior people inside and outside Anthropic on the gaps they expose

• Hire, manage and develop a team and a bench of facilitators

• Make the program scalable: maintain a library of tested scenarios that the team reuses most of the time, refreshed on a regular cadence so they stay timely

• Build a facilitator kit ("TTX in a box") so other internal teams or external partners can run exercises to the same standard

• Create and direct the tools behind the exercises, including Claude-driven simulations that generate a live outside-world feed during play

Minimum qualifications

• Have designed and run tabletop exercises, wargames, or simulations for senior decision-makers and published on the subject

• Have training in a discipline that uses simulation, experimental methods or structured analysis

• Have 10+ years of experience in national security, government, technology policy, or strategy

• Can keep the scenarios technically grounded with a strong grasp of AI capabilities and safety research

• Have managed a team, including hiring, setting direction, giving feedback and developing people

• Use Claude and other AI tools extensively in your own work

• Care about AI safety and Anthropic's public benefit mission

Preferred qualifications

• Published research on wargaming methods, simulation or crisis decision-making

• Run exercises that fed into real policy or crisis-response decisions

• Run multi-iteration or experimental wargames and analyzed results across runs

• Used AI agents or language models as players, adjudicators or analysts in simulations

• Led a research program or team through a period of growth

• Existing relationships across national security, government, policy and AI, and are trusted in those communities

• Published widely read work on AI, emerging technology, strategy or crisis decision-making

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

$295,000—$295,000 USD

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.title: Lead Functional Safety Engineer
jobs.description:
About Dexterity
Dexterity is the enterprise Physical AI company building intelligent robots for complex industrial work.
Dexterity's Mech systems combine the Foresight World Model, robotics, and a Physical AI platform to perform demanding logistics workflows - including trailer loading, trailer unloading, and airport baggage handling - at the speed, reliability, and safety levels required for high-volume operations. Dexterity's Foresight World Model powers real-time perception, planning, and execution across physical environments with the interpretability required for industrial deployment. Dexterity is headquartered in Redwood City, California.
Dexterity is backed by world-class investors such as Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Obvious Ventures. We are a diverse and multidisciplinary team with a culture built on passion, trust, and dedication.
About the Role
Lead functional safety engineering for industrial robots, autonomous mobile systems, and motion-control and drivetrain architectures. Own the full safety lifecycle — from hazard and risk analysis through requirements, architecture, implementation, verification, and validation — to support compliant deployment in North American, European, and Japanese markets.
Responsibilities
- Create and maintain a Functional Safety Management Plan. Lifecycle, responsibilities, required work products, competence and independence requirements, and approval authority.
- Develop and maintain Quality Management System (QMS) integration. Define how safety activities, reviews, approvals, deviations, corrective actions, and audits run within the existing quality processes.
- Perform machinery risk assessments per ISO 12100; identify hazards, define safe states and safety functions, and determine required Performance Level (PLr) or Safety Integrity Level (SIL).
- Support compliance and certification activities with certification bodies, test laboratories, and external assessors, including UL, TÜV, NRTLs, notified bodies, and other relevant organizations.
- Interpret relevant regulations and standards, advise engineering teams on their practical application, and maintain awareness of changing robotics-safety and compliance expectations
- Develop and review safety architectures for E-stop, protective stop, Safe Torque Off (STO), safe stopping, safely limited speed, overspeed protection, brake control, restart prevention, and protective sensing.
- Apply ISO 13849-1/-2 and IEC 62061, including redundancy, diagnostics, MTTFd/PFH calculations, common-cause failure analysis, and validation.
- Analyze robotic and drivetrain failure modes, including motor and inverter faults, welded switching devices, encoder or feedback loss, brake, steering, and gearbox failures, unintended torque, overspeed, and loss of control.
- Define safety interfaces among safety PLCs, robot controllers, servo drives and inverters, motors, brakes, encoders, scanners, contactors, and safety I/O; specify safe behavior for communication loss or invalid data.
- Apply safety-rated communication protocols such as PROFIsafe, CIP Safety, and EtherCAT/FSoE, with working knowledge of PROFINET, EtherNet/IP, and other industrial networks as system interfaces.
- Perform HARA, FMEA/FMECA/FMEDA/DFMEA, fault tree analysis (FTA), fault injection testing, and safety-case analyses; translate results into traceable safety requirements and design evidence.
- Perform mechanical and structural analysis. Failure analysis for components whose failure can create or worsen a hazard, linked to inspection and proof-test needs.
- Plan and execute verification and validation activities covering stopping performance, response time, sensor and encoder faults, drive faults, communication loss, restart behavior, and achievement of the defined safe state.
- Support safety-related PLC and embedded implementation, component selection, IEC 61131-3 programming, customer-site standard operating procedures, and scalable safety training and troubleshooting.
- Engage in customer-facing technical meetings to clarify safety design decisions, explain FuSa compliance, and provide expert guidance on system guardrails
Regulatory requirements
- ISO 12100 — Machinery risk assessment and risk reduction.
- ISO 13849-1/-2 — Safety-related parts of control systems: design principles and validation.
- IEC 61508 - foundational, cross-industry functional-safety standard for electrical, electronic, and programmable electronic safety-related systems.
- IEC 62061 — Functional safety of machinery control systems; IEC 61508 — Functional safety of electrical/electronic/programmable electronic (E/E/PE) systems, where applicable.
- IEC 60204-1 / NFPA 79 — Electrical equipment of machinery.
- ISO 10218-1/-2 and ANSI/RIA R15.06 — Industrial robot and robot system safety requirements.
- ANSI/RIA R15.08 and ISO 3691-4 — Industrial mobile robot and driverless industrial truck safety; ANSI/ITSDF B56.5, where applicable.
- IEC 61496 — Electro-sensitive protective equipment; UL 1740 and UL 3100, where applicable.
- Applicable market requirements, including the EU Machinery Regulation and EMC requirements, plus North American certification requirements
Qualifications Required
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, or a related engineering discipline.
- 10+ years of functional safety experience in robotics, autonomous systems, industrial automation, automotive, aerospace, or other safety-critical machinery domains.
- Hands-on experience with servo drives, inverters, motor controls, encoders, brakes, safety PLCs, safety I/O, and safety-rated networks.
- Demonstrated ownership of the complete safety lifecycle: hazard and risk analysis → safety requirements → PLr/SIL determination → architecture → implementation → verification → validation.
- Ability to evaluate manipulator and mobile-platform/drivetrain hazards, including stopping distance, stored energy, braking, unintended motion, and loss of control.
- Experience with Structured Text, Ladder Logic, and/or Function Block Diagram, along with PLCs, microcontrollers, and safety-related embedded systems.
- Functional safety certification such as TÜV Functional Safety Engineer, CFSE, CFSP, or CMSE preferred.
Candidates must be able to determine how a safety-critical failure is detected, how the system reaches a defined safe state, and how the required PL/SIL is quantitatively justified and demonstrated through analysis, implementation, and validation.
What Makes You Successful
- Strong independent ownership, cross-functional communication, and the ability to convey technical safety decisions to engineering leadership and non-technical stakeholders.
- Ability to develop clear compliance documentation, safety procedures, and customer-facing technical guidance.
- Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.

jobs.title: Senior Supply Chain Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

You will design, build, and own the compliance program for K2 Space’s supply chain. You will be the subject matter expert in supply chain compliance best practices for space hardware, building a compliant, resilient supply base that gives us a competitive advantage, owning compliance readiness so programs stay on track for build and delivery targets, and coaching team members to work to the same high standards. Key skills include a deep understanding of export controls (ITAR/EAR), government contract flowdowns (FAR/DFARS), counterfeit parts prevention, and supplier compliance qualification requirements, plus the ability to turn complex regulations into practical processes the team can follow. You will work closely with procurement, quality, legal, engineering, programs and external suppliers to deliver hardware that meets cost, schedule, quality and regulatory requirements for our company-critical missions.

Responsibilities

• Build and maintain the supply chain compliance program, including policies, procedures, training and audit processes that scale with the company

• Partner with procurement and supplier development engineering to onboard suppliers, verify compliance, and maintain records

• Maintain supplier templates, onboarding documentation, supplier questionnaires, and procurement compliance forms

• Ensure procurement transactions comply with company purchasing policies

• Review and ensure correct application of standard Purchase Order Terms & Conditions, quality clauses, shipping requirements, and procurement language

• Manage export control compliance in the supply chain, including ITAR/EAR requirements for technical data sharing, supplier eligibility and international sourcing

• Build compliance metrics and reporting that give leadership clear visibility into supply chain risk and program readiness

• Support proposal activities by providing supplier compliance information, approved supplier data, sourcing inputs, and procurement compliance documentation

• Act as the compliance partner for procurement, quality, legal, engineering and programs on sourcing and supplier decisions

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Law, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience in supply chain compliance management in aerospace and defense

• Strong working knowledge of ITAR, EAR, FAR and DFARS as they apply to procurement and suppliers

• Experience building or scaling compliance programs, including writing policies, procedures and training

• Experience with counterfeit parts prevention, supplier qualification and contract flowdown management

• Experience leading supplier audits, risk assessments and corrective action processes

• Strong attention to detail and the ability to turn complex regulations into clear, practical guidance

• Clear communication skills, with the ability to influence suppliers and internal teams at all levels.

Nice to Have

• Experience supporting DCMA, DCAA or prime contractor audits

• Experience in the space industry or with satellite or launch vehicle programs

• Experience at a startup or fast-growing company where you built compliance processes from scratch

• Comfort working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment with high ownership and little structure

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $130,000 - $165,000 + equity in the company

• Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Export Compliance

As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”

The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). The person hired for this role must therefore either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15 or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license.

Equal Opportunity

K2 Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with K2 Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

Robinhood is seeking a Senior Manager, Valuation to lead and execute valuation analyses for private company investments, minority equity stakes, and other illiquid financial instruments held across the organization. This role will partner closely with Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting (TAFR), Corporate Development, and the RHV Private Markets Valuation Committee to ensure valuations are well-supported, defensible, and compliant with US GAAP (ASC 820, ASC 321/323) and SEC reporting requirements. This role reports into Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting (TAFR) leadership and works closely with the RHV Private Markets Valuation Committee.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, New York, NY, and Chicago, IL office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

Financial Modeling & Valuation Analysis

• Build and maintain complex financial models (DCF, comparable company/precedent transaction analyses, OPM/PWERM, Monte Carlo simulations) to support fair value measurements of private company investments and other illiquid holdings.

• Perform quarterly and event-driven valuations for private equity/venture-style investments, including waterfall/allocation analyses across complex capital structures (preferred stock, SAFEs, convertible notes, warrants).

• Develop and refine valuation methodologies in line with AICPA Private Equity and Venture Capital Valuation Guidelines.

Governance & Reporting

Cross-Functional Partnership

• Advise on the accounting and valuation implications of new or complex investment structures (e.g., tiered/contingent consideration, equity-linked instruments).

Process & Controls

• Drive continuous improvement of valuation templates, market data inputs, and benchmarking practices.

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.

• 10+ years of relevant experience in valuation, financial modeling, investment banking, or private equity/venture capital, with a focus on private company or illiquid investment valuation.

• Demonstrated expertise in building and auditing complex financial models (DCF, comparable company analysis, option pricing models, waterfall/allocation models).

• Strong working knowledge of US GAAP fair value measurement guidance (ASC 820) and its application to private investments.

• Excellent communication skills, with experience presenting valuation conclusions to committees, auditors, or senior stakeholders.

• Advanced proficiency in Excel/financial modeling; familiarity with valuation software or platforms a plus.

Solving this challenge isn't just about energy—it's about unlocking the future of AI.

At Verse, we're building the energy intelligence platform for the AI economy. Our software helps the world's largest energy consumers achieve faster, cheaper, and cleaner power by combining real-time control of energy assets with complete visibility into their energy portfolio. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, Coatue, and NVIDIA, and built by pioneers in grid-scale batteries, energy markets, and enterprise software, we're redefining how the world's most ambitious organizations access and manage energy.

The Role

Verse operates a growing fleet of IoT-connected battery energy storage systems under a demanding availability SLA — with contractually committed response windows as tight as 30 minutes for critical incidents. To maintain that standard, we need a sharp, technically curious Fleet Operations Specialist working West Coast hours to serve as the first line of defense during the daytime and evening support window (10:00 AM – 6:00 PM PT).

You will be the first hire in this function at Verse, working alongside another technical subject matter expert, and partnering daily with engineering, data science, product, BizOps, and our customer’s NOC team.  Your start date will align closely with the first waves of a BESS fleet migration onto Verse’s battery management platform, so you'll learn each site as it's commissioned and help write our playbooks from real issues, from the start.

This is a genuinely unique position. On a quiet day, you are a Network Operations Center (NOC) operator — eyes on our fleet dashboard, monitoring uptime, site health, and system telemetry across distributed battery installations. When something needs attention or sites are coming online, you become a front-line commissioning expert and troubleshoot installations, logging the issues, triaging severity, working through a structured troubleshooting playbook, and escalating as needed with peer teams to regain critical system operations.

Further, this role has growth-path opportunities to build observability tooling and, automated remediation scripts, and AI-assisted workflows — from a searchable knowledge base built from every resolved ticket, to automated alert triage, to one-click fixes for recurring issues — reducing manual break-fix work over time.

Your job is to resolve as much as possible at the front line, make engineering escalations rare and easy, and to keep our customers confident that Verse is watching.

Key Responsibilities

• Fleet Monitoring & NOC Operations: Monitor real-time health, uptime, connectivity, and telemetry across Verse's battery fleet. Think like a battery asset manager on critical days and during market or program events. Track per-site and fleet-wide availability against SLA targets, and help build early SLA dashboards and KPI trackers. Log anomalies and tune alerting logic and thresholds to reduce noise and speed up detection.

• Site Commissioning & Migration: Onboard new sites to the platform, including site details, tariffs, program enrollments, and meter/asset topology. Validate configurations and automated checks during software cutover. Coordinate sign-off and manual testing with the customer's NOC before automated optimization goes live, and capture lessons-learned from each migration batch to streamline the process.

• Customer-Facing Support: Serve as the first point of contact during the back half of our 8:00 AM – 9:00 PM ET support window (10:00 AM – 6:00 PM PT). Triage Sev 1–4 issues in Linear and meet response SLAs (30 minutes for Sev 1), with structured, hourly updates on critical incidents. Once trained, join the after-hours on-call rotation as the first page for Sev 1 incidents.

• Technical Troubleshooting: Remote into site controllers to work through a structured playbook covering versions, connectivity, logs, configurations, and autonomous operation. Apply networking and energy-domain judgment to separate hardware, software, and optimization issues. Resolve what's within scope. Otherwise, escalate to Engineering & Data Science (Tier 2) with a complete handoff package, pull in Energy Storage SMEs and Product as needed, and follow up on OEM and vendor tickets.

• Operational Support & Documentation: Maintain runbooks, SOPs, and response and handoff templates, and build a knowledge base from every resolved ticket so issues are solved once and eventually automated. Support root cause analyses and the monthly performance report with BizOps, flag Risk Register patterns, and identify repetitive tasks for scripting or automation.

What We're Looking For (Minimum Qualifications)

• 3–5 years of experience in a technical support, NOC, field service, or IT operations role.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills — you will be the voice of Verse to enterprise customers during incidents.

• Working knowledge of networking fundamentals: IP addressing, VPN/tunneling (e.g. Tailscale), connectivity diagnostics (ping, traceroute, port checks), and common failure patterns.

• Ability to read and interpret software logs, system status outputs, and basic telemetry data to form a diagnostic hypothesis.

• Highly organized with a process-oriented mindset; you follow a checklist and document as you go — and improve the checklist when it falls short.

• Ability to work independently and make sound judgment calls in a fast-moving environment, particularly during incident windows when much of the team is offline, and Support will need to decide if/when to escalate.

• Genuine interest in energy and battery storage, and willingness to learn how battery dispatch, tariffs, and grid programs drive system behavior. Prior energy industry experience preferred. We will provide additional training specific to batteries.

• Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation for critical incidents, including occasional evenings and weekends.

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

• Experience in a NOC, data center operations, or infrastructure monitoring role.

• Familiarity with IoT systems, SCADA, or industrial control software.

• Exposure to energy storage, solar, or grid-connected hardware systems.

• Experience with site commissioning, field deployment, or system cutovers/migrations.

• Scripting experience (Python, Bash, or SQL) to automate routine checks

• Experience building knowledge bases or using AI tools to streamline support workflows (familiarity with Knowledge-Centered Service is a plus)

• Coursework or certification in networking, systems administration, or IT.

• Experience supporting or interfacing with software engineering teams on bug reproduction and escalation.

What Makes Verse a Great Place to Work?

• Lead with Empathy: We lift each other up with humility and kindness, always putting colleagues and customers first

• Be Honest & Transparent: We prioritize effective communication to build trust with our team, customers, and stakeholders

• Move with Balance & Precision: We believe speed and perseverance must be accompanied by thoughtfulness and reflection

• Leave the World a Better Place: We are passionate about our mission, and we strive to create a sustainable world for future generations

Base Pay Range

$85,000 - $120,000

This is the estimated base salary range for this position, which does not include the value of benefits or a potential equity grant. A wide range of factors are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to level, skill sets, market conditions, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and business and organizational needs.

Benefits and Employee Perks

• Diverse and inclusive working environment
