jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Applied Research
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Chakra Labs' mission is to encode human taste into intelligence. We build high-fidelity environments, evals, and datasets for frontier AI research, working with several of the top labs.

Our work sits at the frontier of post-training, agent environments, data quality, and research infrastructure. We care about building systems that make models better in ways that are measurable, useful, and hard to fake.

 


WHAT YOU’D WORK ON

 - Post-training loops. You’d help design and run model improvement workflows across supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning approaches like GRPO. The work is not just launching training jobs; it’s figuring out what signal matters, how to collect it, and whether the model actually improved.

 - Environment and task design. We build environments that feel real and scenarios that push agents past static benchmark behavior. You’d design tasks, tools, validators, reward signals, and evaluation harnesses that test meaningful capabilities instead of whatever is easiest to measure.

 - High-fidelity trajectories. You’d create, inspect, and improve the data that teaches models how to behave. That means caring about taste, correctness, edge cases, and whether a trajectory would actually help a frontier model learn.

 - Reward and evaluation systems. You’d work on reward functions, rubrics, validators, and analysis tools that turn messy model behavior into useful training signal. You should be interested in where evals lie, where rewards get hacked, and how to make measurements more robust.

 - Training and research infrastructure. You’d run experiments across distributed GPU clusters, work with PyTorch and FSDP, and build the infrastructure needed to support model training, evaluation, and data generation at scale.

 - Customer research problems. You’d work with frontier AI labs to translate ambiguous research goals into concrete environments, datasets, experiments, and deliverables.

 


ABOUT YOU

 - Machine learning fundamentals. You have Masters / PhD-level knowledge of machine learning fundamentals. You understand linear algebra, optimization, stochastic gradient descent, and can reason from first principles when a model or training run behaves unexpectedly.

 - Hands-on post-training experience. You have worked with or deeply understand LLM fine-tuning, preference data, reward modeling, or reinforcement learning for language models. You know the difference between reproducing a recipe and understanding why it works.

 - Environment-building instinct. You are excited by agent environments, multi-turn tool use, sandboxed tasks, eval harnesses, and the question of how to test capabilities that do not fit neatly into a benchmark.

 - Python and PyTorch fluency. You are strong in Python and comfortable building with PyTorch, FastAPI, and modern ML infrastructure. You can work at a high level, but you are also comfortable dropping into lower-level primitives when the abstraction leaks.

 - Strong engineering judgment. You can move between research ambiguity and production constraints. You know when to iterate quickly, when to be rigorous, and when a result is too fragile to trust.

 - Experience. No hard rule. Roughly 3-5 years is what we imagine, but more or less experience works if the expectations above resonate with you.

 


WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

 - The work is concrete. You are not just “touching the latest AI stack.” You are building the environments, trajectories, evals, rewards, and training loops that frontier labs use to improve models.

 - It is research-facing, but production-minded. Our customers are AI researchers and labs pushing the edge of what agents can do. The systems you build need to support real experiments, real users, and real deadlines.

 - Ownership, not theater. You own whole problems, not isolated tickets. One week you might be designing a new environment; the next you might be debugging a training run, improving a reward function, or scaling an eval pipeline.

 - Ambiguity is part of the job. There is no fixed playbook for this work. Data, post-training, and agent evaluation are changing quickly. If you need every problem to be fully specified before you begin, this role will be challenging.

 - The team. Our team is ex-Stripe, Snap, AWS, Microsoft, Airtable — you'll work with a small team who has years of shipping high-impact products over the last decade.

jobs.title: Product Design Manager
jobs.description:
What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than  3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

About the Role

We are hiring a design lead: a player-coach for someone who still loves to design while also having a passion to make other designers better.

This role sit within Roo’s product team, which owns product and design craft across the company. The product team supports a number of squads (aka business units), the cross-functional teams accountable for driving the success of the key pillars of our marketplace. Designers are aligned to one or more squads to deliver meaningful business impact but formally sit within the product team to ensure we are creating a cohesive product experience across squads. Holding that tension well is at the core of this job.

As a player-coach, you'll spend real time in Figma owning a few projects end-to-end to drive measurable business impact for one or more business units. At the same time, you’ll help set the quality bar across our full product surface by defining what design excellence means at Roo, and making it stick. You'll grow and coach the team, raise the craft, and build the practices that let design scale with the company.

This role is remote, with occasional travel to our San Francisco co-working space for key meetings and team events.

Responsibilities

• Lead, mentor, and grow the 5 person Product Design team. Support designers in developing strong craft, critical thinking, and strategic influence.

• Evolve our design competencies into a standard the whole company can understand and then make it operate. Today that bar largely lives in people's heads. Making it explicit, defensible, and consistently applied.

• Support career growth by running development conversations, writing performance reviews with business-unit leaders, and making the path from one level to the next clear

• Take on real design work yourself. Everything from hard problems, quick wins, exploratory concepts, and the things that unblock the team.

• Partner with leadership to align design direction with product strategy and company goals.

• Build and strengthen design systems that enable consistency, quality, and scalability. This includes raising the team's leverage with AI by helping to drive forward efforts to make our design system agentic-friendly so prototypes can be built from real components.

• Shape design practices across discovery, concept development, interaction design, prototyping, and delivery.

• Encourage exploration and push the team to rethink assumptions while staying grounded in user needs and market realities.

• Advocate for the customer experience across every surface and ensure design decisions always reflect real customer needs.

Qualifications

• 8+ years of product design experience with 2+ years of management experience

• Demonstrated ability to grow, coach, and support senior designers in improving their craft and helping them extend their skillset from strong execution toward strategic influence

• Strong portfolio demonstrating excellence across visual design, interaction design, systems thinking, product storytelling, and user centered craft.

• Experience building and scaling design systems.

• AI fluency in design practice. You've used AI to move faster on real work and you have a considered view on where it helps and where it produces work that shouldn't ship.

• Ability to bring clarity to ambiguous spaces and turn loose ideas into compelling product concepts.

• Strong cross functional communication skills and experience working closely with cross-functional leadership

• Experience with a variety of user research methods. You know how to get answers from users yourself and help your designers do the same.

• Excitement about shaping the future of the industry by designing experiences that support meaningful work.

• Experience leading design across multiple products or surfaces. Two-sided marketplace experience is a strong plus.

Core Values

Our Core Values are what shape us as an organization and we're looking for people who exhibit the same values in their professional life; Bias to Urgency, Drive Measurable Impact, Seek Understanding, Solve Customer Problems and Have Fun!

What to expect from working at Roo!

For permanent, full time employees, we offer:

Overall, you would be part of a mission-driven company that will significantly empower the lives of all veterinary professionals and the health of the overall animal industry that seeks massive innovation.

jobs.title: Laboratory Technician
jobs.description:
The Laboratory Technician is primarily responsible for performing laboratory tests and analyses under the direction of a lab supervisor or scientist including specimen management, specimen pipetting, instrument operation/maintenance, data entry and specimen storage with a high degree of proficiency. Follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Ensure all laboratory equipment and work areas are clean, sterile, and in proper working order. May be responsible for calibration of instruments. Conducts routine tasks as directed. Closely supervised with little latitude for independent judgment.

Laboratory Technician Duties Include but are not Limited to the Following:

• Examine samples for validity and other requirements (sample type, volume, etc.)
• Perform sample preparation steps which may include specimen pipetting with a high degree of accuracy and precision
• Operate, calibrate and maintain all assigned laboratory equipment and instruments according to standard operating procedures to ensure quality results
• Perform reagents and materials preparation for testing
• Maintain adequate inventory of supplies, reagents and materials needed for testing
• Document remedial action, troubleshooting, quality assurance activities and instrument maintenance
• Adhere to established processing timelines
• Perform data entry into the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
• Label samples and deliver them to proper area(s)
• Retrieve and re-file samples for testing
• Properly store specimens for short term and long term storage
• Aid laboratory personnel in cleaning duties
• Adhere to all quality and safety standards, as well as ensuring compliance with all applicable regulatory agencies
• Adhere to policies and protocols in the lab
• Work closely and communicate with other lab associates to complete daily activities efficiently
• Represent department and the organization favorably and in accordance with established Company standards and associate attributes at all times
• Other duties as assigned by management

Basic Minimum Education Qualifications:

• BS or BA in Biological, Physical, or Chemical Science
• OR BS or BA degree in related science fields with 16 hours in Biology, 16 hours in Chemistry and 3 hours of Mathematics

Basic Minimum Work Requirements:

• Minimum 1 year data entry experience preferred
• Previous clinical laboratory experienence preferred
• Experience or formal training in working with potentially infectious human blood bodily fluids preferred
• Ability to work with automated and manual platforms
• Must possess skills required for aseptic techniques
• Intermediate level of proficiency with PC based software programs
• Ability to read, interpret, and comply with documents such as internal SOPs, operating and maintenance instructions, and company policies
• Position may require evening and weekend hours
• Goal oriented, with excellent time management and organizational skills
• Excellent interpersonal skills, with ability to interact effectively and work efficiently with people at all levels in the organization
• Excellent verbal & written communication skills
• Keenly attentive to detail
• Ability to keep sensitive information confidential
• Intermediate level of proficiency with PC based software programs, with database skills
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.

Physical Requirements:

• Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate a keyboard and other office equipment, use a telephone, access file cabinets and other items stored at various levels, including overhead
• Ability to speak and hear well enough to communicate clearly and understandably with sufficient volume to ensure an accurate exchange of information in normal conversational distance, over the telephone, and in a group setting
• Ability to stand for extended periods of time as necessary in the laboratory (4 or more hours)
• Ability to lift and move items weighing up to 15 pounds
• Physical dexterity sufficient to move body frequently around laboratory equipment and instrumentation
• Ability to continuously operate a personal computer for extended periods of time (4 or more hours)
• Mental acuity sufficient to collect and interpret data, evaluate, reason, define problems, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, make valid judgments and decisions

The essential physical and mental requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Position is full-time working Tuesday - Saturday, 2:00pm - 10:30pm, additional hours as needed. Candidates currently living within a commutable distance of Lenexa, KS are encouraged to apply.

• Excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, dental, and vision options
• Life and disability insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid vacation and holidays

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Containers
jobs.description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

Who we are

Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role, in a nutshell

Chainguard Containers is our core product, and this team builds it. As Principal Software Engineer in Container Product Engineering you will be the most senior individual contributor on a team of about fifteen engineers, setting the technical direction for the product and leading its largest, most consequential projects from idea to customer.

Chainguard is growing explosively. Every line of code is now written with AI in the loop, which means the foundation it runs on has to be secure by default. You will shape that foundation: the hardened container images, the registry that serves them, and the tooling that lets engineers and AI agents adopt them.

This is a technical leadership role, not a management role. You will work directly with engineering and product leaders to form the roadmap, then lead engineers across sub-teams to execute it. You will stay hands-on: you write and review code every week, and the hardest problems land on your desk first.

What the team owns

• Product features for Chainguard Containers. Letting customers push their own images to our registry, Custom Assembly (customers compose images from our hardened packages), Helm charts, notifications, and compliance views such as STIG dashboards (STIG is the US government's hardening standard).

• The image build pipeline. The systems that turn packages from Wolfi, our Linux distribution, into signed and attested container images at scale, including moving image builds onto our own runner infrastructure.

• Registry performance and distribution. Work such as lazy loading, so a container starts before its whole image has downloaded, and image signing with Sigstore.

• Adoption tooling for engineers and AI agents. Migration tools that convert existing Dockerfiles to Chainguard Containers, and MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets AI agents call tools) so agents can discover and pull our images directly.

What you'll do

• Set the technical direction for Chainguard Containers: the architecture of the build pipeline, the registry, and the adoption tooling over the next one to three years, written down and defended in the open.

• Form the roadmap with engineering and product leaders, then execute it. Turn ambiguous business goals into sequenced, staffed technical plans, and own the delivery of the largest multi-team projects from concept through production and adoption.

• Make and own the trade-offs that shape the product: build versus buy, when to re-platform and when not to, what to cut to hit a date. Write the decision down and bring dissenting engineers along.

• Lead through other engineers. Set the design bar, review the designs and code that matter most, and grow the Staff and Senior engineers around you into the next generation of technical leaders.

• Work with AI coding agents as part of how you build, review, and operate, and set the standard for how the whole team uses them safely as volume grows.

• Follow a problem wherever it goes: another team's service, a customer escalation, a support ticket, or go-to-market data, and work across team and company boundaries to get ahead of planning cycles.

• Represent Chainguard in the container and open source ecosystem: upstream work, standards conversations, talks, and the customer conversations where credibility is the product.

• Keep the systems you own healthy: observability, on-call, and the structural fixes that stop whole classes of incidents.

What we're looking for

• 10+ years building and operating software that paying customers use, including several years as the technical lead of large, multi-team projects at a startup or a company in hyper-growth.

• Closely relevant experience in what we do: container images, container registries and the OCI image format (Open Container Initiative, the standard for container images and registries), Linux distributions or package management, build systems, or software supply chain security.

• Known in the field. Your work is visible outside your employer: open source you maintain, standards you helped shape, talks or writing that other engineers cite, or systems the industry knows you built.

• A track record of technical leadership without authority: you have set direction for a team you did not manage, and the team delivered.

• Experience forming and executing roadmaps with engineering and product leaders, including saying no, re-sequencing, and holding a date.

• Judgment on trade-offs at the product level. You have made calls that moved a company's roadmap, and you can show what you gave up and why.

• A systems thinker who designs for the whole path, from upstream source through build, signing, distribution, and the customer's runtime, and who sees second-order effects before they land.

• High agency and urgency. You find a way, you do not wait to be unblocked, and you unblock others.

• AI-native in how you build and lead. You use agentic coding tools daily and you have changed how a team works because of them.

• Architectural depth in Go: you can design a Go service from scratch, plus strong API design, databases and caching, and cloud infrastructure on GCP or AWS.

• Low ego. You do what you say and say what you do, and you communicate early when the news is bad.

• Excellent written English and experience leading on a distributed, remote-first team.

Nice to haves

• Deep software supply chain security background: SBOMs (software bill of materials), Sigstore signing, or SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts, a framework for build integrity).

• Maintainer of, or significant contributor to, Chainguard's open-source tools (Wolfi, apko, melange) or neighboring projects such as containerd, Kubernetes, or OCI specifications.

• Experience taking a product from early customers to broad adoption.

• Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code experience.

• A non-traditional path into engineering. We value people who learned by building.

Location

Remote. United States preferred; Open to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or relocation for this role.

Explore Our Work

Dive into the practical side of what we do at Chainguard. These resources provide a hands-on look at our processes and offer an opportunity for in-depth understanding of our product offerings and the technology behind them.

• Chainguard Academy

• https://www.chainguard.dev

Base Salary Range

$229,000—$258,000 USD

About Us

We live and breathe our company values:

• We are customer obsessed — We focus on delivering solutions to our customers that create value and make their lives better.

• We have a bias for intentional action — We prioritize, plan, try things, and fail fast.

• We don't take ourselves too seriously (but we do serious work) — We are solving an important problem which takes focus, but we also like to enjoy the journey.

• We trust each other and assume good intentions — We're transparent with decisions to empower team members to make well informed decisions.

A few of the benefits we offer:

• Flexible & Remote-First Culture: Work remotely with team meetup opportunities, bi-annual destination summits, and a monthly stipend for coworking spaces, phone and internet costs.

• Our Approach to Equity: Receive stock options upon hire and promotion. Plus, you can participate in secondary offerings and have 10 years to exercise your options (yes, you read that correctly: 10 years!).

• 100% Covered Health Insurance: We cover 100% of your health, vision and dental insurance premiums for you and your dependents. Nothing comes out of your paycheck.

• ∞ Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need – to do our best work, we need to recharge and reset.

• 18 Weeks Paid Parental Leave: We offer 18 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents, with the option to use it all at once or throughout your child's first year.

If your experience is close but doesn't fulfill all requirements, please apply. We're building the best team in technology and are focused on hiring "Chainguardians" with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.

Chainguard is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Chainguard will process your personal data in accordance with Chainguard's Global Candidate Privacy Notice.

©2026 Chainguard. All Rights Reserved.

jobs.description:
About the Team

Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models, ensuring our models are deployed responsibly and have a positive impact on society. Our work spans diverse research and engineering initiatives—from system-level safeguards and model training to evaluation and red-teaming—all aimed at mitigating misuse, misalignment, and maintaining our high bar for safety. We lead OpenAI's commitment to developing and deploying safe Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), fostering a culture of trust, responsibility, and transparency. Our goal is to continuously learn from deployments, distribute AI’s benefits widely, and ensure that powerful tools remain aligned with human values and safety considerations.

Within Safety Systems, the Model Policy team works to ensure that frontier models behave safely and reliably in real-world environments by designing policies that define safe model behavior.

We've had several relevant publications, including:

 - Safety at every step https://openai.com/safety/

 - OpenAI GPT6 System Card https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-astra

 - OpenAI Model Spec https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-model-spec/



About the Role

We’re hiring a Model Policy Manager to shape model behavior for U.S. government use, with a focus on national security applications. You’ll define nuanced policies and translate them into training and evaluation criteria, helping models navigate high-stakes scenarios while preserving their usefulness and capabilities.



In this role, you’ll:

 - Develop model policies that guide safe and useful behavior.

 - Build evaluations, identify policy gaps and model failures, and use findings to improve policies and training.

 - Work with research, engineering, and domain experts to support safe, reliable deployment.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring relevant experience in AI safety, policy, or risk assessment.

 - Have strong judgment and can turn complex safety questions into clear, practical policies.

 - Have the technical fluency to work hands-on with model data and evaluations.

jobs.title: Senior Director, R&D Planning & Operations
jobs.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

We are looking for a seasoned operations leader to run the financial and workforce operating engine for Okta's Product & Technology organization — a 2,000+ person R&D function spanning the Okta Platform (ORD) and Auth0. The team is accountable for the budget and workforce strategy components of the R&D Operating Plan, program spend and budget governance, financial compliance including Capitalized Software and R&D tax credit capture, vendor operations, and headcount governance in partnership with Recruiting. The team also runs the annual goal-setting process and the operating cadence that tracks R&D performance against those goals. This is a role that demands real depth in engineering finance operations alongside the organizational judgment to translate executive strategy into a defensible budget and a credible hiring plan.

This role sits within Okta's R&D ("ORD") organization, reporting to the Head of Strategy & Operations and Chief of Staff to the President of Okta R&D. This role is hub-based: it sits in San Francisco, Seattle or Chicago, and candidates must live within commutable distance of one of those offices. We expect this leader to work from the office multiple days each week.

Job Duties / What This Role Entails

• Own the budget and workforce strategy components of the R&D Operating Plan, translating corporate strategy and the long-range plan into a fully resourced annual plan across ORD and Auth0.

• Direct R&D budget governance for a 2,000+ person organization — program spend oversight, variance reporting, fiscal discipline, and executive-level budget reviews with the President of Okta R&D and Finance leadership.

• Own and evolve the P&L framework for R&D lines of business, arming executive leadership with the cost and investment data behind portfolio decisions.

• Model, govern and optimize AI token spend across the P&T organization — establish the cost baseline and forecasting model, build the framework for measuring return on that spend, and partner with engineering leaders to drive efficiency as consumption scales.

• Lead engineering cost modeling, and partner with FP&A and Deal Desk on account-specific margin analysis to support pricing, packaging and large-deal decisions.

• Own financial compliance for R&D, including Capitalized Software entries and maximizing US/Canada R&D tax credit capture.

• Build and own the P&T expense data platform on Snowflake to enable clean line-of-business cost distribution and self-service cost visibility for engineering leaders.

• Set the fiscal year workforce strategy in partnership with Recruiting leadership — headcount governance, real-time allocation tracking, backfills, organizational growth mapping, and location strategy.

• Own the contingent workforce program end to end, including contractor and agency lifecycle, capacity and spend.

• Own vendor operations for R&D — third-party relationships, capacity management, contract renewals, and performance SLAs.

• Continuously refine the financial and workforce operating processes to eliminate friction and ensure the organization scales efficiently as it grows.

• Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to develop the fiscal year goals and OKRs for the R&D organization, and run the program cadence — monthly and quarterly reviews — that gauges performance against them.

• Set the standard for AI-first operations — apply AI to financial analysis, dashboard generation and workflow automation, and build a team for which AI fluency is core to how the work gets done rather than an experiment on the side.

• Build, mentor and develop the operations team as a source of durable advantage for Okta R&D, including hiring and developing Director-level leaders.

This is a team leadership role with five direct reports.

Qualifications / Who You Are (Must Have)

• 12+ years of work experience, including 6+ years leading business operations, R&D / engineering operations, or FP&A functions within a technology company.

• Demonstrated ownership of an engineering or R&D budget at scale — annual planning, in-year governance, variance management, and executive budget review.

• Proven ownership of workforce planning and headcount governance in close partnership with Recruiting and Finance.

• Experience managing a vendor portfolio, including contract negotiation and renewal, SLA management, and capacity planning.

• Hands-on experience with Capitalized Software accounting and R&D tax credit programs in the US and/or Canada.

• Strong understanding of B2B SaaS business models and engineering cost structures.

• Track record of building and developing high-performing operations teams, including hiring and developing Director-level leaders.

• Extensive experience navigating complex data sets and operating with ambiguity, where clean data is not available.

• Demonstrated use of AI to do the substance of finance and operations work — analysis, reporting, dashboard generation and workflow automation — with a clear point of view on where to apply it next.

Qualifications / Who You Are (Good to Have)

• Experience operating across multiple product units or post-acquisition entities with distinct financial and operational systems.

• Experience modeling or governing consumption-based spend, such as cloud infrastructure or AI / LLM token usage.

• Experience with global workforce and location strategy, including India-based engineering centers.

• Experience running an annual goal-setting or OKR process for a technology organization, including the review cadence that tracks progress against it.

• Prior experience in FP&A, management consulting, or a central strategy and operations function.

• MBA, or an undergraduate degree with a concentration in Finance, Economics, Statistics or Engineering.

Why this role?

• Strong executive sponsorship from Okta's product and engineering leadership team.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Product
jobs.description:
ABOUT BRETTON AI

Bretton runs AI-native operations for the financial back office. OCC, Fed and FDIC regulated banks use Bretton AI to run compliance, risk, fraud, and operations on one platform, on their own data and policies, with every output traced, cited, and audit-ready.

We’ve raised over $95M from Greylock, Y Combinator, Thomson Reuters Ventures and other top tier investors. We’re based in downtown San Francisco and our team comes from world-class organizations like Google, Netflix, Stripe, Plaid, Brex, and more.




THE ROLE

We’re hiring Product Engineers who excel at turning complex customer problems into elegant technical solutions. You’ll own substantial features from conception to production, working directly with customers to understand their needs, designing scalable architectures, and shipping code that measurably improves compliance operations.

This role combines deep technical work with high customer impact. You’ll build systems that process thousands of cases, save compliance teams significant time, and directly contribute to company revenue.




WHAT YOU’LL BUILD

 - Develop intuitive interfaces for case management, reporting, and analytics.

 - Build document analysis and verification systems.

 - Build agentic workflows that coordinate AI tools and data services to perform research, enrichment, and verification, while keeping humans in the loop for review.

 - Create tools that help customers configure and customize their compliance workflows.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR




MUST-HAVES:

 - 4+ years (Engineer) / 6+ years (Sr. Engineer) / 8+ years (Staff Engineer) of experience building production software.

 - Strong full-stack capabilities, including backend services, APIs, databases, and (nice-to-have) frontend development.

 - A track record of shipping customer-facing products where reliability is critical.

 - An end-to-end ownership mindset, from requirements gathering through deployment and iteration.

 - Clear communication skills—you can explain technical decisions to diverse audiences.

 - Product thinking—you understand why you’re building something, not just how.




VALUED EXPERIENCE:

 - Building workflow engines, orchestration systems, or process automation tools.

 - Working in regulated industries where compliance, auditability, and data integrity are critical.

 - Integrating AI/LLM capabilities into production applications.

 - Creating configuration systems, admin tools, or workflow builders for non-technical users.

 - Designing systems for multi-tenancy, versioning, or complex authorization models.

 - A strong foundation in data modeling and distributed systems.




TECHNICAL SKILLS:

We work with a mix of TypeScript, Python, Node.js, React, cloud infrastructure, and workflow orchestration frameworks. You don’t need prior experience with our exact stack, but you should be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and applying them in production.

jobs.title: Security & IT Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT SOFAR OCEAN

Sofar Ocean is building the world's largest real-time ocean sensor network. Our Spotter buoys collect ocean data across the globe, and our software, including Wayfinder for voyage optimization, turns that data into decisions for commercial shipping, government, and defense customers. We're a team of about 100 based at Pier 28 in San Francisco, and we're growing fast.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll own Sofar’s corporate security and identity infrastructure and lead our security compliance program. You’ll turn security priorities into working controls, and be the internal point person for customer security reviews. Helpdesk and facilities IT are handled by our managed IT partner, whom you’ll work alongside.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Identity and access: own Google Workspace as our identity provider. Roll out SSO and SCIM provisioning across our SaaS tools, automate joiner/mover/leaver processes, and run periodic access reviews.

 - Endpoints: own device management (MDM, EDR) and endpoint detection and response, including device compliance policies.

 - Security operations: tune and triage SIEM detections. Track vulnerability remediation across Dependabot findings and pen test results. Maintain and exercise our incident response plan.

 - Compliance: run day-to-day work toward SOC 2 and other compliance processes. That includes maintaining policies, operating our compliance platform, collecting audit evidence, and reviewing vendors and subprocessors.

 - Customer trust: own responses to customer security questionnaires and assessments. Keep our answers accurate, consistent, and defensible.

 - Vendors: manage day-to-day relationships with our managed IT provider, security vendors and advisors, contractors, and auditors.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years in IT systems, corporate security, or security engineering, ideally at a startup

 - A clear, well-reasoned point of view on how a ~100-person startup should approach security, including where to invest early, where to accept risk, and how to sequence compliance work. You can defend that view and adjust it when the context changes.

 - Hands-on administration of Google Workspace and an SSO/SCIM stack, plus MDM and EDR tooling

 - Working knowledge of AWS IAM. Scripting ability in Python or similar for automation.

 - Has been through at least one SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit from the inside

 - Writes clearly and precisely. You prefer a defensible claim to an optimistic one.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience Vanta or Drata, AWS CloudFormation, Auth0

 - experience with SIEM detection engineering




LOCATION, COMPENSATION, & BENEFITS

 - The preference is for this role is based at our Pier 28 office in San Francisco a few days a week to work seamlessly with our team. However, we are open to remote applicants.

 - The base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $200,000, plus equity. Final pay depends on experience and skills. We offer medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), flexible PTO, and a learning and development stipend.

 - The range listed is what we reasonably expect to pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and may be modified in the future. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, experience, and equity package.




OUR APPROACH TO AI IN THE HIRING PROCESS:

At Sofar, we use AI tools in our day-to-day work, and we don't expect our hiring process to be any different. Here's how we think about it:

Applying: Write your own first draft — we want to hear your voice and understand your real experience. AI is fine for refining and polishing, not for generating your story.

Take-home assessments: Complete these on your own unless we've explicitly said otherwise. We'll always be upfront about it when AI is allowed.

Interview prep: Go for it. Use AI to research Sofar, practice your responses, and sharpen your thinking before we meet.

During interviews: This is you. We're a small team and we move fast — live conversations are how we get to know you, and we're genuinely curious how you think in real time.

A note on transparency: We're a lean People team, and we use AI to help with things like drafting job descriptions, preparing interview questions, and candidate communications. We don't use it to make hiring decisions — those are always ours.

The through line: use AI to show more of yourself, not less :)

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas and retain an immigration lawyer to support the process. While we can't guarantee sponsorship for every role or situation, if we make you an offer, we'll make every reasonable effort to make it work.

A note on applying: We mean it when we say we want the strongest people — not the most credentialed ones. If you're excited about this work but don't check every box, please apply anyway. Research consistently shows that underrepresented candidates are more likely to self-select out, and that's a loss for everyone. Sofar operates at the intersection of ocean science, climate, and technology — the problems we're solving are consequential, and the perspectives we bring to them matter. We're actively working to build a team that reflects that.

• Logical, sequenced thinking. You can articulate dependencies and the order in which work must happen.

• Comfort with AI and agentic workflows across modern GTM tools.

jobs.title: Director of Demand Planning
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Thrive Market is seeking a Director of Demand Planning to lead demand forecasting, strengthen our Sales & Operations Planning process, and expand the planning tools that support our supply chain.

This role combines deep analytical expertise, hands-on systems building, and strong cross-functional leadership. You’ll translate business inputs into actionable forecasts, build and enhance models in Anaplan, and bring teams together around a shared plan for execution.

You’ll join a smart, collaborative, low-ego team with the opportunity to shape how we work. We have a strong weekly forecasting foundation in place. Your opportunity is to build on that foundation, broaden its impact across the company, and develop tools that connect demand to inventory, fulfillment, transportation, and capacity decisions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Own the demand forecasting process, incorporating historical performance, seasonality, promotions, assortment changes, and business trends to support inventory availability and operational planning.

• Track forecast accuracy and bias, investigate variances, and refine models and assumptions to improve the quality of planning decisions.

• Build and lead a cross-functional S&OP cadence that connects demand, supply, operational capacity, and financial goals. Surface risks, align stakeholders on tradeoffs, and drive clear decisions and accountability.

• Take a hands-on role in enhancing demand forecast models in Anaplan and developing supply chain planning tools, including labor planning, transportation shipment forecasting, corrugated material forecasting, and space planning.

• Collaborate with Merchandising, Marketing, Growth, Finance, and Operations to gather inputs, challenge assumptions constructively, and maintain a shared view of expected demand.

• Translate forecast changes into clear implications for purchasing, staffing, transportation, and fulfillment capacity. Ensure stakeholders understand what has changed, why it matters, and what actions are needed.

• Set priorities, coach team members, and strengthen analytical capabilities while increasing the demand planning team’s visibility and influence across the business.

• Establish clear planning assumptions, reporting, documentation, and workflows that support growth while remaining practical and adaptable.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Demonstrated success leading demand planning or forecasting in e-commerce, grocery, consumables, subscription commerce, or a similarly complex business with recurring demand and seasonal variability.

• Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including experience developing forecasting models, evaluating forecast accuracy and bias, and translating complex data into business decisions.

• Hands-on experience building and enhancing Anaplan models, with the ability to translate business needs into practical planning tools.

• Experience building or strengthening an S&OP process and connecting demand forecasts to inventory, capacity, financial planning, and operational execution.

• Strong cross-functional relationship and influencing skills. You can bring together stakeholders with different priorities, challenge assumptions respectfully, and build alignment around a shared plan.

• A builder mentality and comfort working with evolving systems and processes. You enjoy identifying gaps, testing solutions, and creating a playbook as the business grows.

• Experience leading and developing a planning team while staying close to the data, models, and day-to-day work.

• Clear communication and sound judgment, with the ability to explain complex findings, surface risks early, and recommend actionable next steps.

BELONG TO A BETTER COMPANY

jobs.description:
About Kalepa:

Insurance is a $7T global industry built on professional labor: underwriting, claims, pricing, operations, and distribution. Kalepa is building AI that can perform that work.

We create professional-grade AI systems for insurers: software that can read, reason, decide, and act inside real workflows and operate over long-time horizons. Kalepa begins by augmenting professionals with the tools to succeed at their jobs. That earns us the right to learn from real decisions, capture decision traces, and automate what can be automated successfully over time.

Our products are already in production with leading insurers, driving measurable outcomes and expanding across functions. The opportunity is far broader than any single workflow: to build the AI operating system for decision-making across insurance. For people who want to work on AI that matters, in a sector where correctness, trust, and real-world impact count, Kalepa is just getting started.

Kalepa is backed by leading investors such as IA Ventures and Inspired Capital, and our team brings experience from Facebook, Palantir, Google, Amazon, McKinsey, Mastercard, and Uber.

Our Values (This is important):

Many organizations have a dusty list of corporate values that no one ever follows. Kalepa is not one of those companies. Our values are designed to unlock the potential of our employees.

Success at Kalepa is bred from five core principles:

• Hustle and Determination - We hire people who take full ownership of their craft and relentlessly pursue excellence with speed and determination. We choose the hard problems and do not give up. This is the foundation of how we work and how we win.

• Deliver Customer Impact - We're obsessed with customer impact. Every feature, every line of code, every decision is measured against one question: does this help insurers make better decisions? If it doesn't drive speed, accuracy, or profitability for our customers, we don't build it.

• Meritocracy - We're building something exceptional, and that requires exceptional people and ideas. We have a high bar but we reward excellence with rapid growth. If you're the best at what you do, you'll thrive here.

• Transparency - We value honest, transparent communication over politics. We challenge ideas, not people. We say what needs to be said, even when it's hard. This is how we solve problems fast and find the truth.

• Experiment Relentlessly - Many of the problems we face have never been solved before. We tackle them by testing quickly, measuring rigorously, and iterating until we find the path forward. Speed of learning is our advantage.

In addition to our NY office, we have remote employees speaking 10+ languages across the globe. But we invest in bringing our people together both for regional meetups and global offsites (2021 - Playa Del Carmen | 2022 - Rome | 2023 - Buenos Aires | 2024 - Lisbon | 2025 - Cartagena).

Kalepa’s culture isn’t for everyone, and that’s ok. But for the people who are a fit, they can’t imagine working elsewhere.

jobs.title: Administrative  Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Blueprint

Blueprint is a technology solutions firm headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with teams across the United States. We help organizations turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes by connecting strategy and execution across AI, cloud, data, product development, and emerging technology.

Our culture is built by people who care deeply about doing exceptional work. We set high standards, take ownership, and continually challenge ourselves and one another to be better. We work hard, support each other, and take genuine pride in what we deliver for our clients, partners, and teams.

At Blueprint, you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.

Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.

In This Role

In this role, you will support the end-to-end management of business guest credentials for a large enterprise organization. You will serve as a primary point of contact for business guests, managers, administrators, and internal stakeholders, ensuring requests are handled efficiently and information remains accurate and up to date. Your responsibilities will include coordinating onboarding and offboarding, tracking credential renewals and end dates, responding to inquiries, and assisting with access and IT-related needs. You will also coordinate device requests and returns when needed and provide support for additional credential management activities. This remote role is well suited for an organized, detail-oriented professional who enjoys structured administrative work, clear communication, and keeping day-to-day operations running smoothly.

Responsibilities

• Coordinate the end-to-end business guest credential management process, including onboarding, offboarding, renewals, and credential end dates.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for business guests, managers, administrators, and internal stakeholders regarding credential-related questions and requests.

• Monitor shared inboxes, respond to email inquiries, and ensure requests are triaged, tracked, and resolved in a timely manner.

• Maintain accurate business guest records, credential information, status updates, and tracking reports.

• Assist business guests with onboarding-related access issues and basic IT support needs, coordinating with appropriate support teams when necessary.

• Coordinate device requests, distribution logistics, and device returns while maintaining accurate records.

• Communicate updates, outstanding actions, and potential delays to relevant stakeholders to ensure visibility and consistent follow-through.

• Support additional credential management activities, administrative requests, and ad hoc operational tasks as business needs evolve.

Required Qualifications

• At least 2 years of experience in administrative support, business operations, coordination, or a related role.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage inquiries and coordinate effectively across multiple stakeholders.

• Excellent organizational and time management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage recurring tasks, competing priorities, and deadlines.

• Demonstrated ability to maintain accurate records, track requests, and follow established processes through completion.

• Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information.

• Ability to work independently in a remote environment while maintaining a consistent schedule and responsive communication.

• Reliable follow-through, a proactive approach to managing inboxes and requests, and the ability to identify items requiring additional attention.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting administrative operations within a large enterprise, corporate, or technology-focused organization.

• Experience coordinating employee, contractor, vendor, or business guest onboarding and offboarding.

• Familiarity with credential lifecycle management, access requests, account administration, or identity and access management processes.

• Experience managing shared inboxes, service requests, tracking logs, status reports, and stakeholder communications.

• Experience coordinating IT equipment requests, device distribution, returns, or inventory tracking.

• Experience using Excel and SharePoint to maintain records, manage documentation, and track operational activities.

• Experience supporting process-driven workflows that require accuracy, confidentiality, consistency, and minimal supervision.

• Relevant hands-on experience in administrative or business support; a degree is not required in place of applicable experience.

Compensation

At Blueprint, we strive to offer competitive pay that reflects the value of our team members. Compensation for this role is influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, education, responsibilities, experience, and geographic market.

The anticipated compensation range is $15 to $16 per hr. Please note that we typically do not hire new employees at the top of the posted range. Actual starting pay will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. The final compensation and job title may vary depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications.

Benefits

Blueprint believes that healthy, supported employees do their best work. Eligible employees have access to a comprehensive benefits package that may include:

• Medical, dental, and vision coverage

• Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

• 401(k) retirement plan

• Competitive paid time off

• Parental leave

• Professional growth and development opportunities

Benefits and eligibility may vary based on role, employment status, and location.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Blueprint Technologies, LLC is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital or familial status, military or veteran status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in any part of the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@bpcs.com.

jobs.description:
About Kalepa:

Insurance is a $7T global industry built on professional labor: underwriting, claims, pricing, operations, and distribution. Kalepa is building AI that can perform that work.

We create professional-grade AI systems for insurers: software that can read, reason, decide, and act inside real workflows and operate over long-time horizons. Kalepa begins by augmenting professionals with the tools to succeed at their jobs. That earns us the right to learn from real decisions, capture decision traces, and automate what can be automated successfully over time.

Our products are already in production with leading insurers, driving measurable outcomes and expanding across functions. The opportunity is far broader than any single workflow: to build the AI operating system for decision-making across insurance. For people who want to work on AI that matters, in a sector where correctness, trust, and real-world impact count, Kalepa is just getting started.

Kalepa is backed by leading investors such as IA Ventures and Inspired Capital, and our team brings experience from Facebook, Palantir, Google, Amazon, McKinsey, Mastercard, and Uber.

Our Values (This is important):

Many organizations have a dusty list of corporate values that no one ever follows. Kalepa is not one of those companies. Our values are designed to unlock the potential of our employees.

Success at Kalepa is bred from five core principles:

• Hustle and Determination - We hire people who take full ownership of their craft and relentlessly pursue excellence with speed and determination. We choose the hard problems and do not give up. This is the foundation of how we work and how we win.

• Deliver Customer Impact - We're obsessed with customer impact. Every feature, every line of code, every decision is measured against one question: does this help insurers make better decisions? If it doesn't drive speed, accuracy, or profitability for our customers, we don't build it.

• Meritocracy - We're building something exceptional, and that requires exceptional people and ideas. We have a high bar but we reward excellence with rapid growth. If you're the best at what you do, you'll thrive here.

• Transparency - We value honest, transparent communication over politics. We challenge ideas, not people. We say what needs to be said, even when it's hard. This is how we solve problems fast and find the truth.

• Experiment Relentlessly - Many of the problems we face have never been solved before. We tackle them by testing quickly, measuring rigorously, and iterating until we find the path forward. Speed of learning is our advantage.

In addition to our NY office, we have remote employees speaking 10+ languages across the globe. But we invest in bringing our people together both for regional meetups and global offsites (2021 - Playa Del Carmen | 2022 - Rome | 2023 - Buenos Aires | 2024 - Lisbon | 2025 - Cartagena).

Kalepa’s culture isn’t for everyone, and that’s ok. But for the people who are a fit, they can’t imagine working elsewhere.

jobs.title: Mechanical Safety Engineer
jobs.description:
Eurofins Food & Feed Testing is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to develop practical engineering solutions that eliminate workplace hazards across our laboratory network.

This position focuses on designing, validating, and implementing engineered solutions that enhance employee safety while maintaining (or improving) process quality and operational performance. Working closely with laboratory operations, maintenance teams, quality personnel, and EHS professionals, the Mechanical Engineer will transform identified hazards and operational challenges into scalable engineering controls that can be deployed across multiple laboratories. This role is a cornerstone of Eurofins' commitment to achieving best-in-class OSHA safety performance across our Eurofins Food & Feed Testing network.

The ideal candidate enjoys solving real-world problems through engineering design, prototyping, equipment modification, ergonomics, automation, and process improvement. Success in this role will be measured by the quality, effectiveness, and adoption of engineered solutions that reduce employee exposure to risk while supporting efficient laboratory operations.

• Design and develop engineering controls that eliminate or reduce workplace hazards.

• Apply mechanical engineering principles to improve safety, ergonomics, material handling, and equipment operation.

Develop solutions including:

• Mechanical lifting and handling devices
• Ergonomic workstation improvements
• Equipment modifications

• Custom fixtures and tooling

• Machine guarding and protective systems

• Automated handling solutions

• Process redesigns

• Specialized laboratory equipment

Develop and Validate Solutions

• Lead projects from concept through implementation.

• Create engineering drawings, specifications, and design packages.

• Develop prototypes and proof-of-concept solutions.

• Perform testing and validation activities to verify performance and effectiveness.

• Troubleshoot design challenges and refine solutions based on operational feedback.

• Support installation, startup, and deployment activities.

Drive Enterprise Improvements

• Evaluate recurring hazards and operational challenges occurring across multiple laboratories.

• Develop standardized engineering solutions suitable for network-wide deployment.

• Create implementation guides, engineering standards, and best practices.

• Partner with operations teams to ensure solutions are practical, maintainable, and effective.

Manage Projects

• Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and implementation plans.

• Coordinate activities with equipment suppliers, fabricators, machine shops, contractors, and internal stakeholders.

• Support capital project development and business case preparation.

• Manage multiple projects simultaneously from concept through completion.
• Other duties as assignd.

Required

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related course of study.

• 5+ years of engineering experience involving equipment design, product development, manufacturing systems, process improvement, automation, or related fields.

• Demonstrated experience taking projects from concept through implementation.

• Strong mechanical aptitude and practical problem-solving skills.

• Experience working with fabrication vendors, machine shops, equipment suppliers, or maintenance organizations.

• Excellent communication and project management skills.

Preferred

• Experience with CAD software such as SolidWorks, Inventor, AutoCAD, or similar.
• Experience with prototyping and product development.
• Experience with ergonomics, human factors engineering, or material handling systems.
• Experience in laboratory, food manufacturing, pharmaceutical, industrial, or regulated environments.
• Familiarity with automation, robotics, machine guarding, or industrial equipment.
• Familiarity with validation activities and change management processes.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work!

What Success Looks Like

• Engineering solutions successfully deployed across multiple laboratories.

• Reduction of employee exposure to high-risk tasks and activities.

• Development of practical, sustainable controls that improve both safety and operational efficiency.

• Successful completion of projects on schedule and within budget.

• Adoption of standardized engineering solutions across the laboratory network.

• Measurable improvements in employee safety, ergonomics, and workflow performance.

This role offers a unique opportunity to solve meaningful engineering challenges that directly impact hundreds of employees across one of North America’s largest food testing laboratory network.

You will have the opportunity to design equipment, improve processes, develop new technologies, and create practical solutions that make laboratory work safer, easier, and more efficient. The Lead Clinical Quality Documentation Specialist reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine (NM), adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

• The Lead Clinical Quality Documentation Specialist is a Registered Professional Nurse and expert Clinical Documentation Specialist, responsible for leading clinical documentation integrity efforts in support of NM and business unit strategic goals under the direction of Clinical Documentation program leadership. The Lead Clinical Quality Documentation Specialist is proficient in clinical documentation integrity and quality concepts and is responsible for initiatives leading to cross-regional change and program enhancements. The Lead Clinical Quality Documentation Specialist anticipates issues, interprets internal / external issues, and helps lead problem resolution by aligning resources, recommending best practices, and implementing related solutions. Key to this role is also the ability to lead and facilitate verbal and written conversations with key stakeholders across NM as well as oversee and coach clinical documentation team members through challenging projects or issues. The Lead Clinical Quality Documentation specialist is a change agent that systematically drives and implements documentation and coding program improvements that leads to accuracy and improved performance to advance financial and quality outcomes for NM and each business unit. May require travel to support the business needs of Northwestern Medicine. The Lead Clinical Quality Documentation Specialist applies advanced knowledge of the national quality agenda and clinical documentation integrity best practices to advance problem analysis and creative process redesign for Northwestern Medicine.

Responsibilities:

• Masters the art and science of Clinical Documentation and serves as a resource and role model for staff.
• Collaborates with Managers of Clinical Documentation, the Director of Clinical Documentation, and Medical Director leadership to align clinical documentation integrity work efforts to the extent possible throughout NM.
• Collaborates with leaders across NM to advance Clinical Documentation work efforts. Key Stakeholders include, but are not limited to, Managers of Clinical Documentation, Director of Clinical Documentation, System Clinical Coding Leaders, Business Unit and System Clinical Quality Managers and Directors, Business Unit Nutrition Managers, Business Unit Clinical Managers.Scope includes all functions which support documentation within the patient’s medical record. Scope includes all practitioners, clinicians and others participating in delivering or supporting patient care, including those privileged through the medical staff, trainees, students, employees, volunteers.
• Applies knowledge of professional practice, Clinical Documentation standards, best practices, and interdisciplinary collaboration to advance problem analysis and resolution and creative process redesign.
• Advanced understanding of clinical documentation through the lens of local and national quality and ranking methodologies, including but not limited to, U.S News and World Report, Vizient, Leapfrog, the CMS Star Rating, and payer contracts and assists the Managers of Clinical Documentation in implementing key strategies to teach and deploy the team in the manner necessary to effect change.
• Leverages NM network to initiate conversations, identifies root causes and resolution, and aligns resources.
• Teaches and coaches colleagues on all areas of clinical documentation integrity and independently assists in the onboarding of new staff.
• Instructs Clinical Documentation team and distributes updated information on Clinical Documentation and Coding concepts, federal rule changes, and risk methodology updates.
• Performs medical record reviews and other data collection activities that assist in identifying potential documentation issues and opportunities for improvement.
• Analyzes case review data to accurately and cogently reflect patterns and trends that require improvement.
• Collaborates with Clinical Documentation program leadership to determine individual physician and/or service line educational needs.Creates and presents targeted physician education in collaboration with Clinical Documentation program leadership.
• Participates in key strategies for the review and reporting of DRG denials, Patient Safety Indicators (PSIs) and Hospital Acquired Conditions (HACs) as assigned.Supports the monthly report-out of PSI and HAC events at each business unit as requested.
• Leads, plans, and coordinates the Clinical Documentation Integrity onboarding process at the business unit and system level.Collaborates with manager to assist with interviewing of new team members, posting of new requisitions, and coordination of onboarding.Develops and evaluates initial and ongoing orientation and training programs to establish and monitor competencies.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer - Veza
jobs.description:
About Veza

Veza is the identity security platform for human, non-human, and AI agent access. Customers use it to see who and what has access to what, govern it, and remediate risk across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem systems.

Agent security is the inflection point. Static access reviews can't keep up with autonomous agents acting at machine speed. Security is shifting to continuous, real-time control: just-in-time access for agents, automated remediation of policy violations, and real-time governance of agent actions as they happen—replacing standing privileges and periodic reviews.

Veza is in transition, growing quickly as part of ServiceNow's Security & Risk organization. The Chief Architect will shape how the platform scales to meet this new category.

What you'll do

• Own the end-to-end architecture of the Veza platform, including the access graph, ingestion pipeline, authorization and policy engine, and the services built on them. Lead the evolution toward a graph-native data model (Neo4j or equivalent) that scales to billions of relationships and complex permission hierarchies. Set the standards every team builds to.
• Lead the next-generation data architecture. Evolve the core graph and storage model for order-of-magnitude growth in customers, entities, and relationships, with a clear migration path from today's system and no customer disruption.
• Define the architecture for non-human identity and AI agent security. Make Veza the system of record for what agents can access, and design for governance, guardrails, and auditability.
• Set the AI architecture for Veza's own agents and features: agentic patterns, evaluation, observability, cost and capacity planning, and a multi-vendor LLM strategy that avoids lock-in.
• Modernize the integrations framework. Veza has 300+ integrations, and they drive a disproportionate share of support load. Establish a scalable, testable, self-service framework that raises reliability and cuts onboarding time.
• Architect how Veza fits into ServiceNow. Veza is not built on the ServiceNow platform. Define the integration model, shared identity and data contracts, and UI surfacing patterns that deliver a unified customer experience without forcing a rewrite.
• Drive deployment flexibility: multi-region SaaS, data residency, regulated-industry requirements (e.g., EU financial regulation such as DORA), and federal-grade deployment, including the compliance and operational constraints each brings.
• Govern architecture across teams. Run architecture reviews, manage tech debt and the security backlog, and make clear, documented build-vs-buy and sequencing decisions.
• Raise the bar on engineering practice, including heavy use of AI coding agents, automated testing coverage, defect escape reduction, and operational excellence with SRE.
• Represent Veza's architecture to executives, customers, partners, and ServiceNow architecture and security leadership.
• Mentor architects and senior engineers and build the next layer of technical leadership.

What you bring

Core

• 15+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years as a staff/principal/chief architect, or equivalent, over a large multi-team platform.
• Deep experience designing multi-tenant, cloud-native SaaS at enterprise scale: distributed systems, large-scale data and graph systems, APIs, and microservices.
• Hands-on Kubernetes and cloud experience (AWS required; multi-cloud a plus) and modern DevOps, IaC, and SRE practices.
• Strong background in graph databases and data structures. Hands-on experience with Neo4j, or similar graph platforms; understanding of immutable or event-sourced storage models and their operational trade-offs.
• A track record of leading large architectural migrations in a live production system.
• Experience influencing without direct authority across multiple teams and geographies (US, EU, India).
• Executive-level communication, with the ability to write and defend an architecture decision to engineers, customers, and the C-suite.
• Strong proficiency in Python and Go or Java, with the ability to go deep in code and design reviews.

Security and identity

• Strong background in identity and access: IGA, IAM, PAM, authorization models, access reviews, lifecycle management, or adjacent security domains.
• Understanding of non-human identity (service accounts, secrets, API keys, workload identity) and emerging agent identity and authorization models.
• Experience building security products that meet their own security and compliance bar (SOC 2, FedRAMP or equivalent, data residency).

AI

• Experience delivering production AI systems: LLMs, agentic architectures, RAG, evaluation, observability, guardrails, human-in-the-loop, and managing model cost and capacity.
• Active use of AI-native development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent) and the ability to drive adoption across teams.

Preferred

• Experience through an acquisition or platform integration, aligning an acquired architecture with a parent platform.
• Prior experience with integration-heavy platforms (hundreds of connectors) and the reliability challenges they bring.
• Familiarity with graph databases or immutable/event-sourced storage models.
• BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Success in the first 12 months

• A published, org-wide architecture vision and roadmap for the next-generation platform, with committed milestones.
• An integrations modernization plan in flight, with measurable reduction in escalations and onboarding time.
• A defined, adopted pattern for Veza-ServiceNow integration and UI surfacing.
• A sustainable architecture review and governance process the teams actually use.
• Clear architecture for agent and NHI security that product and sales can take to customers.

You’ll report to the Training Lead and act as the primary point of contact for your training deployments—owning classroom delivery, managing logistics, interfacing with customer stakeholders, and upholding the highest standards of professionalism, safety, and instructional clarity.

You will deliver comprehensive training through classroom instruction, hands-on exercises, and live flight instruction, ensuring students develop the technical knowledge, practical skills, and operational proficiency required for successful system employment. You will assess individual performance against standardized evaluation criteria, maintain professional engagement with military leaders and operational teams, and support unit-level training to enhance readiness and capability integration. Additionally, you will contribute to curriculum development, training equipment management, and the continuous refinement of instructional methods through field-informed feedback and operational lessons learned.

This role is remote and requires travel expectations of 50%.

Responsibilities

• Serve as the lead instructor and customer-facing point of contact for all assigned field training operations

• Deliver classroom instruction using standardized Neros curriculum, ensuring engagement and comprehension across varying skill levels

• Coach students through hands-on troubleshooting and system operation while adapting instruction to their skill level, mission needs, and field conditions

• Manage pre- and post-course logistics, including scheduling, site setup, gear preparation, and customer coordination

• Maintain detailed training records, rosters, sign-in sheets, and pass/fail assessments using defined grading criteria

• Submit after-action reports, performance summaries, and feedback to the Training Lead

• Identify trends or challenges in student performance and provide structured feedback to help refine future curriculum

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Mission Success, to ensure training aligns with operational realities and system capabilities

• Provide end user feedback across internal departments to inform product development and drive continuous improvement

• Maintain professionalism and instructional quality across both classroom and range environments

You should have the following

• Prior military experience or experience working with the military (strongly preferred)

• Experience teaching, coaching, or mentoring adults in technical or tactical environments (strongly preferred)

• Possess a valid FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate or obtain certification within 45 days of hire

• Exceptional communication, facilitation, and classroom leadership skills

• Familiarity with FPV systems and UAS operations, including basic air and ground components

• Confidence leading groups in both classroom and field environments, with the ability to adapt on the fly

• Experience using flight simulators as part of training programs (preferred)

• Working knowledge and experience with ATAK (preferred)

• Strong organizational and documentation skills, including grading, reporting, and inventory tracking

• A high level of composure and professionalism in fast-paced or austere conditions

• Initiative and commitment to continuous professional development, with an emphasis on technical and tactical proficiency

• A mission-first mindset, willingness to travel, and a strong sense of ownership over training outcomes
